newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of China sees profit growth for HK banks.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China sees profit growth for HK banks.

text.p: Hong Kong's banking industry is expected to post modestly higher profit growth this year than in 1996 due to improvements in the sector's operating environment, the Bank of China said on Thursday.

Demand for banking services will rise in line with Hong Kong's accelerating economic growth, China's improving economy and Southeast Asia's continuing high growth, the bank said in its Hong Kong-Macau Economic Quarterly research report.
But growing competition will put pressure on interest spreads, thereby raising risks, it said.

Demand for loans will grow notably in 1997, linked to work on Hong Kong's new airport, a brisk property market and a local economic revival as well as infrastructure projects in China and Southeast Asia, it said.

The price war in the mortgage market is expected to continue but not intensify, it said. Despite an increased number of players, competition will be curbed by higher risks in mortgage loans and increased outlets for cash.
Higher demand for loans might lead to a keener quest for deposits, which might raise costs, it said.
Bad and doubtful debts are expected to fall as the economy recovers and the number of bankruptcies wanes, it said.
